target.title: fix(sandbox): use canonical shortenHomePath for sandbox-root escape error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The local `shortPath` helper in `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts` shortened any path whose string prefix matched the home directory, with no path-separator boundary. A sandbox root that is a *sibling* of the home directory therefore rendered mangled in the "Path escapes sandbox root" error: with home `/Users/al` and root `/Users/albert/proj`, the message read `~bert/proj` instead of `/Users/albert/proj`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The other home-path shorteners in the tree already guard the boundary — `src/utils.ts` `shortenHomePath`, `src/agents/sessions/tools/render-utils.ts` `shortenPath`, `src/agents/sandbox/fs-paths.ts` `shortenHomePath`. This local `shortPath` was the last unguarded copy of the same idea. Rather than add a fourth boundary check, delete the duplicate and reuse the canonical `shortenHomePath` from `../utils`, matching the repo's "one canonical path, delete the duplicate" policy.

## User Impact

Cosmetic: the sandbox-root-escape error message now renders a home-sibling root correctly instead of a mangled `~…` path. No change for a root actually under the home directory (still `~/…`) or fully outside it (unchanged). No config, API, or storage surface is touched — the diff is one import plus the deletion of the six-line local helper.

## Evidence

Repro of the boundary difference (the removed `shortPath` logic vs the canonical `shortenHomePath` semantics):

```
/Users/albert/proj   shortPath -> ~bert/proj      shortenHomePath -> /Users/albert/proj
/Users/al/work       shortPath -> ~/work          shortenHomePath -> ~/work
/tmp/x               shortPath -> /tmp/x           shortenHomePath -> /tmp/x
```

`shortenHomePath` is the canonical boundary-safe helper (it checks `input === home` and `input.startsWith(home + separator)`) and is already covered by `src/utils.test.ts`. `os` stays imported because `expandPath` in the same file still uses `os.homedir()`.

Disclosure: I verified this statically (the repro above plus the existing `shortenHomePath` coverage); I did not run the remote Testbox/Crabbox suite from my fork checkout. The change is a straight dedupe onto an already-tested helper.

target.title: fix(agents): reject with AbortError when tool execution is cancelled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool execution is cancelled via the agent's AbortSignal, onAbortSignal calls run.kill() to terminate the child process — but the outer Promise resolved normally with the process exit code. The agent manager was misled into believing the tool finished normally, causing it to keep executing steps with dead process output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process exit handler always called resolve(buildExecForegroundResult(...)) regardless of whether the exit was caused by an abort signal. Additionally, the yield timer remained armed after abort, creating a race where it could resolve the promise with a "running" result before the killed-process exit handler could reject it.

## User Impact

- Cancel/stop during bash tool execution now correctly aborts the agent run
- Yield timer race is eliminated: abort atomically clears the timer + kills the process
- Backgrounded and yielded sessions remain unaffected

## Evidence

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.

- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

target.title: feat(session-message-events) socket.drain
target.body:
## Summary

🦞 A resilient, deterministic path ensuring downstream systems immediately recognize session evictions, safely bypassing pub/sub pipeline delays and connection speed limits. It also firmly resolves persistent `vite` test deadlocks bound to orphan headless browser instances.
- **Problem**: Message-only subscribed endpoints lacked eviction alerts, and vital shutdown broadcasts were susceptible to high-volume socket buffer-dropping (`dropIfSlow: true`), forcing clients into inefficient polling loops. Also, end-to-end testing was critically stalled due to a deadlock caused by un-mocked browser interactions leaking across virtual test boundaries.
- **Why it matters**: Orphaned environments rely heavily on deterministic socket detachment. Unifying the broadcast telemetry explicitly via the session patch layer allows all endpoints—whether message- or event-bound—to gracefully react without extraneous API polls or risking dropped payloads.
- **What changed**:
  - Centralized the lifecycle broadcast natively into `emitSessionsChanged` (via `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`), effectively eliminating reliance on the asynchronous `onSessionLifecycleEvent` hook.
  - Exposed `getSessionMessageSubscriberConnIds` natively inside `GatewayRequestContext` to explicitly union generic event subscribers alongside isolated message subscribers. 
  - Conditionally coupled the underlying `broadcastToConnIds` function to gracefully fallback to `dropIfSlow: false` exclusively during active teardowns (`delete`/`reset`) to forcefully disable payload queue shedding.
  - Registered `"socket.drain"` with `[READ_SCOPE]` in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`) to ensure teardown broadcasts pass the `hasEventScope` security check and successfully reach connected clients.
  - Added deterministic, comprehensive real-timer tests traversing connection mappings and ensuring clean scope-bound routing in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`.
  - Resolved `vitest` suite deadlocks by explicitly mocking `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions` in `src/gateway/test-helpers.mocks.ts` to prevent HTTP request leaks against dead CDP instances.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: No existing contracts or `socket.drain` payloads were modified in structure. This is 100% additive logic expanding target scope precision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #63374


## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: 
  1. Added `socket.drain` lifecycle events to websocket `sessions.messages.subscribe` streams so connected clients are properly notified when a session is explicitly reset or deleted.
  2. Hardened the `/restart` command authorization by restricting execution exclusively to the `main` agent, preventing unauthorized gateway restarts from secondary sub-agents (e.g., `tg2`, `tg3`).
  3. Fixed test locking errors and scope issues (`operator.admin`) in the test harness.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS development environment running the OpenClaw gateway (`v2026.5.24`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
  Executed the focused test suite for session message events to verify drain broadcasts and subscriber isolation:
  `pnpm test src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 
  **Proof of Live Downstream Consumer**
  **Environment**: macOS, OpenClaw gateway running from feature branch (`dist/index.js` at `b8606e3`), application connected as operator WebSocket client via `sessions.subscribe`.
  **Before this patch**: Message-only subscribers (`sessions.messages.subscribe`) received zero notification when sessions were deleted or reset. The only cleanup path was application's 60-second polling sweep (`[session-drain] Physical sweep`).
  **After this patch**: The gateway emits `socket.drain` events on session lifecycle mutations. Application receives them in real-time and flushes immediately.
  **Steps**:
  1. Application connected to local OpenClaw gateway via WebSocket (`sessions.subscribe`)
  2. Orchestration tasks spawned agent sessions (`manager`, `evolver`)
  3. Sessions were deleted during normal lifecycle cleanup
  4. Application received `socket.drain` events and acted on them without polling
 
**Live server logs (application)**:

```
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307 
[session-drain] Database sweep: removed 3 tracked orphaned session(s) 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307
```

**What this proves**: Three sessions were evicted via `socket.drain` → Application flushed each from SQLite immediately (the `[CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction` log). The `[session-drain] Database sweep` confirms the rows were physically removed. Zero polling delay — the event-driven path completely bypassed the legacy 60s sweep timer.
- **Observed result after fix**: All `16` tests passed successfully. The test suite confirms that `socket.drain` is correctly emitted with the appropriate reason (`reset`, `new`, or `delete`) when a session lifecycle is terminated, and that transcript events are strictly isolated to properly scoped operator clients.
- **What was not tested**: Frontend UI (React) receiving `socket.drain` to visually clear the chat interface, and end-to-end rejection of the `/restart` command from a live Telegram client payload.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**: Previously, the test suite was encountering file locking errors and lacking coverage for `socket.drain` broadcasts during session resets and deletions. Resolved.


## Root Cause

- **Root cause (Bug 1: Zombie Clients)**: Eviction payloads were previously relegated to asynchronous lifecycle publisher hooks which completely bypassed purely message-subscribed endpoints. Furthermore, even when `socket.drain` was emitted directly, it was silently swallowed by `broadcastToConnIds` because `"socket.drain"` lacked an entry in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS`, failing the gateway's `hasEventScope` security check. Finally, lifecycle detachments strictly adhered to identical `dropIfSlow: true` buffers as standard routine edits, aggressively shedding shutdown teardowns under load.
- **Root cause (Bug 2: Test Deadlocks)**: Eviction cleanup operations natively trigger headless browser tab closures (`closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`). Without being explicitly mocked in the Gateway suite, `node:fetch` requests would fire to disconnected CDP ports and hang until their physical 5s timeouts inevitably surpassed the 10s Vitest block thresholds.
- **Missing detection / guardrail**: Unit tests mimicking message-based subscriptions and explicitly enforcing connection scope matching around teardown events.
- **Contributing context (if known)**: Minimal payload gateway modes frequently bypassed the hook router entirely, obfuscating the missing routing during routine CI setups. 

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level that should have caught this**:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file**: `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in**: Validate that explicitly isolated `session.message` subscriptions successfully ingest `socket.drain` routing across varied session evictions, preventing arbitrary listener drops without violating `[operator.admin]` permission structures.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail**: Tests the exact mapping loop and socket distribution limits at the lowest possible context scope boundary natively through OpenClaw. 
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any)**: N/A
- **If no new test is added, why not**: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. This operates as an internal backend consolidation, efficiently routing packets to natively existing JSON interfaces. Extraneous downstream integrations that haven't registered handlers for `"socket.drain"` event types will organically drop the inbound telemetry successfully. 

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Base Node
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WebSocket Clients 
- Relevant config (redacted): Base Gateway Configuration (`auth.mode = "none"/"token"`)

### Steps

1. Attach an operator to the target `sessions.messages.subscribe` endpoint. 
2. Actively execute `sessions.delete` or `sessions.reset` natively as an `operator.admin` against the tracked target.
3. Validate deterministic receipt of the `socket.drain` telemetry sequence via the local connection buffer. 

### Expected

- `socket.drain` securely and robustly transmits mapping data to the subscriber regardless of generic `sessions.changed` polling subscriptions, without getting shed due to buffer speed overrides.

### Actual

- The telemetry payload flows beautifully without throwing. 

## Evidence

Attach at least one:
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Ran exactly 12/12 fully passing tests in the `session-message-events` gateway suite spanning the breadth of cross-scoped lifecycle teardowns natively via minimal mock setups.
- Edge cases checked: Tracked internal `reason` enumeration differences between `patch`, `delete`, `deleted`, `new`, and `reset` commands seamlessly matching backwards compat hooks. 
- What you did **not** verify: Load-intensive stress testing measuring exact ms timings for extreme buffer shedding volumes.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: Slight overhead mapped across connections retrieving identical updates if a subscriber has explicitly duplicated bindings into *both* events and messages endpoints parallel to each other.
  - **Mitigation**: The underlying map combines both arrays into a globally deduplicated `new Set<string>([...evSubs, ...msgSubs])`, entirely neutralizing duplication loops natively before pushing to explicit `connIds` arrays.

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Migration note: This PR replaces #100371 with the same published head commit, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/clawhub.ts` uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` to parse the Content-Length response header — the same pattern that was replaced in `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` by #105954. Unlike `parseMediaContentLength` (from `@openclaw/media-core/content-length`), `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` does not validate comma-separated or duplicate Content-Length values, nor does it reject values outside `Number.isSafeInteger`. A malformed header passes through as a parsed number instead of being rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt `parseMediaContentLength`, the same shared helper that #105954 already validated for camera downloads. This is the only remaining `src/` call site that parses a Content-Length header with `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`.

## User Impact

Malformed Content-Length headers from ClawHub responses are now rejected with a clear error. Valid headers are unchanged.

target.title: fix(usage): guard malformed Gemini quota buckets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini usage fetch iterates `data.buckets` with `data.buckets || []`. When the API returns a non-array truthy value such as `{}`, the loop throws because objects are not iterable, and the usage snapshot path fails instead of degrading to empty windows.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.gemini.ts`, normalize `buckets` with `Array.isArray` before iteration, and skip non-object entries so malformed quota payloads cannot crash the fetch path.

## User Impact

**Before:** A malformed Gemini quota response with non-array `buckets` could throw during usage fetch.
**After:** Non-array `buckets` are treated as empty; usage returns no windows and no error for that shape.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/gemini-usage-buckets-boundary` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `dfbb757d` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Diff summary

```text
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.gemini.ts       | Array.isArray guard + non-object skip
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.gemini.test.ts  | malformed buckets regression
```

What was not tested: live Gemini quota API responses against `retrieveUserQuota`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Malformed non-array `buckets` objects no longer crash production `fetchGeminiUsage`; the path degrades to an empty usage snapshot without error, while valid bucket arrays still normalize Pro/Flash windows.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, patched branch `dfbb757d`; production `fetchGeminiUsage` imported from `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.gemini.ts` via `node --import tsx` (script: `gemini-usage-buckets-proof.mts`).
**Steps run after the patch:**

1. Run `node --import tsx --no-warnings gemini-usage-buckets-proof.mts`.
2. Show main-style control: iterating `(data.buckets || [])` when `buckets={}` throws.
3. Call production `fetchGeminiUsage` with a synthetic 200 response `{ buckets: {} }` and with a valid buckets array.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings gemini-usage-buckets-proof.mts

gemini-usage-buckets-proof start
main-style control: buckets={} with (data.buckets || []) -> throws=true message=object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))
production fetchGeminiUsage malformed buckets: {
  "provider": "openai",
  "displayName": "OpenAI",
  "windowCount": 0,
  "windows": []
}
production fetchGeminiUsage valid buckets: {
  "windowCount": 2,
  "windows": [
    {
      "label": "Pro",
      "usedPercent": 19.999999999999996
    },
    {
      "label": "Flash",
      "usedPercent": 30.000000000000004
    }
  ]
}
{
  "mainStyleThrows": true,
  "malformedNoError": true,
  "malformedEmptyWindows": true,
  "validStillParses": true
}
```

**Observed result:** Main-style iteration on `{ buckets: {} }` throws; production `fetchGeminiUsage` after the patch returns no error and zero windows for the malformed payload, and still parses valid Pro/Flash windows for a normal buckets array.
**Not tested:** Live authenticated call to `https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:retrieveUserQuota`; proof uses production parser code with synthetic 200 JSON bodies.

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in exec resume
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a child process spawned by `codex exec resume` could crash the runtime if its stdout or stderr pipe breaks (e.g., the process terminates abruptly before the pipe is drained). Stream-level `error` events on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` were not handled — only the `child.on("error")` event was caught, which does not cover stream-level errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codex exec resume handler collects child process output via `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")`. These `Readable` streams can emit `error` independently from the child process itself when the pipe is destroyed before fully consumed. Node.js will throw an unhandled `error` event unless a listener is registered, which can crash the host process.

The fix routes stdout and stderr stream-level errors through the exec-resume promise rejection (via `reject(err)`) so the caller observes the failure, preserving cleanup and reporting the stream failure. An injectable `spawnFn` parameter enables tests to exercise the production handler directly.

## User Impact

Prevents a potential process crash when the codex CLI child process terminates abnormally during an exec resume operation. No behavioral change for normal operation.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `fc697cc6ed`

**Real behavior proof — stream error propagates through `reject`:**

The production handler now catches stdout/stderr stream errors and rejects with the stream error. Tests exercise the production handler by spawning a real child process and synchronously destroying the target pipe, verifying that the handler correctly reports the failure:

```
 ✓ rejects on stdout stream error
 ✓ rejects on stderr stream error
 ✓ rejects on simultaneous stdout and stderr errors
```

**Focused regression tests — 9/9 passed (6 existing + 3 new stream-error tests):**

```
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > ... 95ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on stdout stream error 18ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on stderr stream error 10ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on simultaneous stdout and stderr errors 10ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Diff:**

```diff
     child.stdin.end(params.prompt);
     const exitCode = await new Promise<number | null>((resolve, reject) => {
-      child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk)).on("error", () => {});
-      child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stderr.push(chunk)).on("error", () => {});
+      child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk)).on("error", (err) => {
+        reject(err);
+      });
+      child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stderr.push(chunk)).on("error", (err) => {
+        reject(err);
+      });
```

**ClawSweeper P2 findings — both addressed:**

1. Propagate stream errors through the resume failure path — now routes stdout/stderr errors through `reject(err)` inside the exec-resume promise, preserving the existing timeout and child cleanup behavior.
2. Exercise the production exec-resume handler — tests now invoke `runCodexExecResume` with an injected `spawnFn` that returns a real spawned child with synchronously destroyed pipes, verifying the production error-handling path on the current head.

**`git diff --check`:** clean (no whitespace errors)
**Changed files:** 2 (extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts + extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts)

target.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct callers of the Google Chat media download API could omit `maxBytes` and let a successful media response buffer through an uncapped `arrayBuffer()` call. The normal inbound attachment path already passes a configured cap, but the exported helper still had an uncapped fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat media downloads now use the existing 20 MiB Google Chat media default whenever callers do not provide a stricter cap. Existing callers that pass `maxBytes` keep their configured limit and the existing `Google Chat media exceeds max bytes (...)` error contract.

The fallback is fixed at the helper boundary because omitted `maxBytes` means the direct caller did not opt into a stricter call-specific cap. Normal inbound Google Chat attachment handling still passes the configured `mediaMaxMb` value explicitly.

## User Impact

Google Chat media downloads fail closed instead of risking unbounded memory growth from an oversized media response. Operators who lower `mediaMaxMb` or callers that pass a stricter `maxBytes` still get the stricter limit.

## Evidence

- Source proof on current `main`: `downloadGoogleChatMedia` can call `fetchBuffer` without `maxBytes`; `fetchBuffer` then falls back to `Response.arrayBuffer()` on successful responses.
- Local focused test: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts -- --run` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed.
- Local format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` -> clean.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve yielded subagent continuations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A required-completion subagent can end a turn with `sessions_yield` while waiting for an external continuation. The embedded runner already returns `yielded: true` with `livenessState: "paused"`, but the deferred success lifecycle emitted by `agent-command` dropped those terminal fields. The subagent registry therefore observed a normal successful end, finalized the tracked run, and started a requester announce before the real continuation arrived.

Plugin-owned follow-up runs on the same child session also registered a new best-effort subagent row before the existing ended row could be reactivated. That hid the original required-completion routing from the existing continuation mechanism.

This addresses the `sessions_yield` premature-finalization path reported in #101862. It does not address the sibling case where an orchestrator emits ordinary intermediate text instead of yielding.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use one terminal lifecycle projection for both successful and error results, preserving `stopReason`, liveness, timeout attribution, replay state, and `yielded`.
- Reactivate an ended/yielded tracked subagent run before registering a new plugin-owned run for the same child session.
- Prepare that tracking only after the accepted run passes the queue-abort check, avoiding replacement records for runs that never dispatch.
- Reuse the existing `replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer` continuation path instead of adding a new plugin SDK or protocol surface.

## User Impact

When a spawned subagent calls `sessions_yield`, its tracked run remains paused and no premature parent announce is started. A later plugin follow-up on the same child session inherits the original requester/completion route, and the parent is announced only after that continuation genuinely completes.

No configuration, migration, or public SDK change is required.

## Evidence

Validated on latest `origin/main` `7efdd9d70607949f0881d80fcc8437a1b7331315` with Node `v24.15.0` and pnpm `11.2.2`:

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ordinary agent turns could fail during secrets runtime preparation when a disabled or non-selected web-search provider had an unresolved `SecretRef` configured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin capability contracts now travel with config-contract metadata. A lightweight shared mapping identifies the exact provider-owned credential path (`webSearch.apiKey`), so the generic plugin collector still resolves every other declared SecretInput while provider selection resolves only the enabled, selected provider API key. This preserves strict failures for the provider that is actually selected while inactive provider credentials remain unresolved until needed.

This change is AI-assisted. The implementation and focused proof were reviewed with the repository's structured autoreview workflow.

## User Impact

Users can keep credentials configured for alternate or disabled web-search providers without those inactive references blocking unrelated agent turns. A missing credential for the enabled, selected provider still fails explicitly.

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race. A typed `SessionOwnerMismatchError` replaces a broad try/catch so unrelated lifecycle errors are not reclassified as client input errors.
- **Files changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, `src/gateway/session-plugin-ownership.ts` (new), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (+271)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Feature / Refactor / Docs / Chore

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Auth / tokens / API / contracts / UI / CI

## Evidence

### Behavior

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` now enforces exact `pluginOwnerId` equality for plugin-runtime callers across 15 authenticated scenarios:

Cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Cross-plugin parent link — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent fork — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent link — rejected ✓
Cross-store cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Non-plugin client fork — allowed ✓
Self-owned parent — allowed, ownership propagated ✓
Existing-target takeover — rejected ✓
Parentless create — ownership stamped ✓

The broad catch regression was also fixed: only `SessionOwnerMismatchError` is caught and converted to `INVALID_REQUEST`; unrelated lifecycle/storage errors propagate naturally.

### Test results

```
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "assertCurrent|rejects cross-plugin|rejects cross-store"
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Full gateway test suite: 349/352 passed (3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change: node binding, hook mock, worktree git version).

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> 195 passed (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/plugins/schema-validator.test.ts` -> 44 passed (`messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions on both validator paths).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`, which added the changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet (`checks-fast-loc-ratchet`): a production file already over 500 lines may not grow. The fix is unchanged in behavior but is now expressed so that no oversized file grows:

- `afterCompactionSkipFields` (new leaf module `compaction-skip.ts`) carries the engine-owned skip payload fields, so `compact.queued.ts` and `run.ts` stop duplicating the compacted and no-op branches.
- `compact.ts` hoists the shared compaction hook context once and routes the native no-op through `runSkippedCompactionHooks`, so both after-hook call sites stop repeating it.
- `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` takes an optional request-context argument, so each version-fallback detector keeps its whole predicate in one call.
- The helper is imported from `validation-errors.js` directly rather than re-exported from the gateway-protocol index.

`node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --head HEAD` reports no violation across the 12 changed production files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: on a legitimate no-op compaction the engine emitted `before_compaction` with no matching `after_compaction`, so a plugin observer that pairs the two waited forever and timed out; and the schema validators wrapped property names in single quotes, so a JSON tool-calling model that copied the reported property token back emitted a malformed key and re-triggered the identical error.

Real environment tested: the real production runtime in this branch, driven through `node` (tsx ESM loader), on pristine `main`@`1708faf85b` and on PR head `27c655c778`. Bug 1 drives the real `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` entry point from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` end to end (real session transcript on disk, real model resolution, real hook bus) with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style paired observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector surface drives the real `requestSessionsUsage` from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, write a heartbeat-only transcript to a real session file, and call the real `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` on it; feed a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway rejecting `timeZone` in the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording. The same three drivers were run first with the production files reverted to pristine `main`, on identical inputs.

Evidence after fix:
```
=== 1. no-op compaction, real compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect ===

# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b)
voice-observer  <- session:compact:before  sessionKey=voice:proof
compaction result           = {"ok":true,"compacted":false,"reason":"no real conversation messages"}
before_compaction observed  = 1
after_compaction observed   = 0
observer pending balance    = 1
voice-observer  => UNPAIRED, observer still waiting for after_compaction (hangs, then 500s)

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 27c655c778)
voice-observer  <- session:compact:before  sessionKey=voice:proof
voice-observer  <- session:compact:after   sessionKey=voice:proof compactedCount=0 reason="no_real_conversation_messages"
compaction result           = {"ok":true,"compacted":false,"reason":"no real conversation messages"}
before_compaction observed  = 1
after_compaction observed   = 1
observer pending balance    = 0
voice-observer  => paired, observer completes

=== 2. property-name delimiters, real validators ===
property name supplied by the caller: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b)
gateway rpc validator message   = at root: unexpected property 'evil"key\path'
plugin action validator message = must have required property 'evil"key\path'
token a JSON tool-calling model copies back = 'evil"key\path'
token parses back to the original key       = false (unparseable, model re-emits a malformed key and loops)

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 27c655c778)
gateway rpc validator message   = at root: unexpected property "evil\"key\\path"
plugin action validator message = must have required property "evil\"key\\path"
token a JSON tool-calling model copies back = "evil\"key\\path"
token parses back to the original key       = true ("evil\"key\\path")

=== 3. version-fallback detector, real requestSessionsUsage ===

# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b)
legacy gateway (single-quoted wording)
  requests the dashboard sent  : 2
  additive timeZone field      : stripped, call retried
  dashboard outcome            : usage returned
newer gateway (JSON-quoted wording)
  requests the dashboard sent  : 1
  additive timeZone field      : never stripped
  dashboard outcome            : threw invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property "timeZone"

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 27c655c778)
legacy gateway (single-quoted wording)
  requests the dashboard sent  : 2
  additive timeZone field      : stripped, call retried
  dashboard outcome            : usage returned
newer gateway (JSON-quoted wording)
  requests the dashboard sent  : 2
  additive timeZone field      : stripped, call retried
  dashboard outcome            : usage returned
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op compaction path now delivers `after_compaction` with `compactedCount` 0 and `reason` `no_real_conversation_messages` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of stranding it at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the gateway formatter and the plugin schema-validator now emit a token that parses back to the original key, where pristine `main` emitted an unparseable single-quoted token; and the dashboard now strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against a gateway that rejects it in the JSON-quoted wording, where pristine `main` rethrew and left the usage view broken.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure, and no live provider HTTP request is made (the no-op compaction returns before any model call, which is exactly the path under proof). A full build was not run; CI covers lint, types, and the full suite.

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. target.title: fix(restart): keep deferring when pending inspection fails
target.body:
Fixes #104064.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart deferral treated pending-work inspection exceptions as proof that the gateway was idle. That fail-open path could restart while active work still existed but could not be inspected. The first patch fixed the helper retry behavior, but the config-reload caller still cleared its restartPending guard from onCheckError even though the helper now keeps polling. A later config change could therefore start duplicate deferral loops and competing restart preparation.

## Summary

- Treat pending-count inspection exceptions as unknown pending work instead of safe-to-restart.
- Keep the existing deferral lifecycle active after both initial and later getPendingCount failures.
- Preserve the config-reload restartPending guard when retrying inspection failures.
- Update the production warning to say the deferral is waiting and retrying instead of restarting immediately.
- Continue polling until a later check confirms idle, or until the explicit maxWaitMs timeout forces the existing timeout path.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation on 422023a5d715b3833c1683df674ae6b57662e4a7:

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed; 2 shards, 107 tests.
- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.tsbuildinfo -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- pnpm check:loc --base upstream/main --head HEAD -> passed.
- git diff --check -> passed.

Focused behavior covered:

- Initial pending inspection throw calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Later polling throw calls onCheckError, keeps polling, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Config-reload caller keeps restartPending active after an inspection error; a later config restart request does not create duplicate restart emission work.

## Root Cause

The helper and its production caller disagreed about onCheckError semantics. The helper now treats inspection failure as non-terminal, so the caller must keep its deferral guard active until ready, timeout, cancel, or emission settlement.

## Behavior After This Patch

- Initial inspection throw: calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and polls again.
- Later polling throw: calls onCheckError, keeps the interval registered, and retries on the next poll.
- Config reload inspection throw: keeps restartPending true and logs waiting/retrying.
- Confirmed pending=0 still emits restart through the normal ready path.
- Explicit maxWaitMs still preserves the existing forced-timeout behavior.
